plan: Economic theory suggests the dominant strategy is to bid my true value of $30. In a single-round game with no repeated interactions, bidding anything less risks losing the item when I could have won, while bidding more risks paying more than the item is worth to me. Since values are independently drawn and this is a one-round game, the recommendation to bid true value seems most rational.

Economic theory suggests bidding exactly my true value of $7 is the dominant strategy in this auction. Since values are redrawn independently each round, strategic manipulation is less effective. Bidding above my value risks losing money if I win, while bidding below risks not winning when I could have. With one round only, the safest approach is to bid my true value of $7, which maximizes my potential profit given the uncertain bids of Andy and Charles.

Economic theory suggests the dominant strategy is to bid my true value of $36. This is because:
1. If I bid less, I might miss winning a prize worth more to me
2. If I bid more, I risk paying more than the item's worth
3. With values drawn independently each round, past rounds don't influence optimal strategy
4. The second-price auction mechanism incentivizes honest bidding
Therefore, I will bid my exact value to maximize potential profit.
